003-vinland.title: The Vikings Reached America First — and We Can Prove It #shorts
lines: Almost five hundred years before Columbus, Vikings sailed to America. At least, that's what the sagas said.
Two Icelandic sagas tell of Leif Erikson finding a land far to the west. They called it Vinland. For centuries, it sounded like a legend.
Then, in nineteen sixty, Helge and Anne Stine Ingstad found a site on the northern tip of Newfoundland. Lahnss oh Meadows.
Under the grass: Norse buildings. Iron rivets. A spindle whorl. A real Viking camp.
And in twenty twenty-one, scientists dated the wood cuts to one year: ten twenty-one. Proven: Vikings were here. Debated: where Vinland really was.

004-heracleion.title: Egypt's Legendary Port Sank Into the Sea. Divers Found It. #shorts
lines: This city sank beneath the sea.
The Greek historian Herodotus wrote of a great port at the mouth of the Nile, where Heracles first set foot in Egypt, and where Paris and Helen of Troy came ashore. Then it vanished.
In two thousand, divers led by Frank Goddio found the city, four miles offshore, about thirty feet down.
Granite statues over five metres tall. A temple of Amun. More than seven hundred anchors, and dozens of shipwrecks.
Proven: the sunken port was real. Debated: whether Helen of Troy was ever here.
